How This Works: The maximum weekly compensation rate in New York is adjusted annually on July 1st. The rate that applies to your case is determined by the date of injury. Benefits are typically calculated as 2/3 of the worker's Average Weekly Wage but cannot exceed the statutory maximum for the year of injury.

2026 NYS Maximum Weekly Compensation Rate

The maximum weekly workers' compensation rate in New York State is $1,281.50 for injuries occurring on or after July 1, 2026, per WCB Subject No. 046-1805. For dates of injury between July 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026, the maximum is $1,222.42.

The rate that governs your case is the one in effect on your date of injury — not the current year's rate. Enter your accident date in the lookup above to see the maximum that applies to your claim.

How New York Sets the Maximum Comp Rate

Under WCL §15(6), the maximum weekly benefit equals two-thirds of the New York State Average Weekly Wage (NYSAWW). The NYSAWW — defined in WCL §2(16) — is the average weekly wage of all workers covered by New York unemployment insurance for the previous calendar year, calculated by the NYS Department of Labor and reported to the Superintendent of Financial Services by March 31 each year.

The new maximum takes effect each July 1 and is announced by the Workers' Compensation Board in an annual Subject Number bulletin. Once set by your date of injury, the maximum rate for your case does not change, regardless of later increases.

How to Calculate Your Weekly Benefit

Your weekly benefit is 2/3 × your Average Weekly Wage (AWW) × your degree of disability, and it cannot exceed the statutory maximum for your injury year. A worker earning $1,500/week who is totally disabled receives 2/3 × $1,500 = $1,000/week. A worker earning $2,100/week hits the cap: 2/3 × $2,100 = $1,400, which is reduced to the $1,281.50 maximum for a 2026 injury.

Start with the free Average Weekly Wage (AWW) calculator to establish your wage under WCL §14. Then estimate permanency awards with the Schedule Loss of Use (SLU) calculator or the Loss of Wage Earning Capacity (LWEC) calculator. For the minimum rate for your injury date, see the benefit rate lookup.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the maximum workers' comp rate in New York for 2026?

For injuries on or after July 1, 2026, the maximum weekly compensation rate is $1,281.50, per WCB Subject No. 046-1805. For dates of injury between July 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026, the maximum is $1,222.42.

How is my weekly workers' comp benefit calculated in New York?

Your weekly benefit is two-thirds of your average weekly wage (AWW) multiplied by your degree of disability, capped at the statutory maximum rate for your date of injury.

Does my compensation rate increase when New York announces a new maximum?

No. The maximum rate that applies to your case is fixed by your date of injury and remains applicable for the life of the case, even as new maximums take effect each July 1.

Is there a minimum weekly compensation rate in New York?

Yes. The minimum weekly benefit rose to $275 on January 1, 2024 and $325 on January 1, 2025, and beginning January 1, 2026 it is indexed to one-fifth of the New York State Average Weekly Wage.

What if two-thirds of my wages is more than the maximum rate?

Your rate is capped at the statutory maximum for your injury year. Higher-wage workers receive the maximum; everyone else receives two-thirds of their average weekly wage at total disability.
